- Trust decision: the unique-job key `md5(class.method.json_encode(data))` is derived only in `QueueManager::getUniqueId`, where `sort($data)` (src/QueueManager.php:307) sorts by value and drops keys, so distinct payloads collide and the second push is silently dropped.
- `pattern_fit`: none — the published fix is one function in one file, and every route into the dedupe sink (push, mailer, requeue CLI, consumption delete) goes through that same helper.
- Strongest lever: the consumption side (`src/Consumption/RemoveUniqueJobIdFromCacheExtension.php:38-42`) re-derives the same ID from the JSON-decoded broker body (`src/Job/Message.php:46`), so a fix placed at the push call site, or one that sorts only the top level, silently breaks duplicate-release.
- Biggest red flag: `tiny_repo` (small plugin, ~40 src files); the O2/O7 serializer asymmetry is real in the code but unexecuted and unconfirmed.
